chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Hamzah al-'Alawi, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Ghalib al-Zurari and Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: Does the menstruating woman make up the salat (prayer)? He said: 'No.' I said: Does she make up the sawm (fasting)? He said: 'Yes.' I said: From where did this come? He said: 'Indeed, the first one who used analogy was Iblis.'

key_terms.إِبْلِيسُ: Iblis, cited here as the first to employ analogy
key_terms.تَقْضِي: to make up an act of worship after its time has passed
key_terms.مِنْ أَيْنَ جَاءَ هَذَا: a question about the source or basis of the ruling

ai.seo_question: Does a menstruating woman make up missed prayers and fasting in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling that a menstruating woman does not make up missed salat (prayer) but does make up missed sawm (fasting). It also points to a rejection of analogical reasoning in deriving this ruling, attributing the first use of qiyas to Iblis.
